transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Priya Kapoor (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Rojas (Halcyon Head of ML), Samir Patel (Halcyon SRE), Nora Kim (Halcyon Product)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping focused on open-model shortlist for Halcyon's document extraction / QA use case in genomics. Discussed success criteria (accuracy on domain extraction, latency SLOs, cost), workload sizing, proposed benchmarks, and 4-week timeline. Decided to run baseline on 3 models and potentially one optimized quantized variant; Redwood to provide harness and security docs.

Topics:
- Success criteria: extraction accuracy, hallucination rate, latency, cost per 10k queries
- Workload sizing: concurrent users, average sequence length, daily QPS
- Benchmarks: QA/NER suite, latency P99, token throughput, memory footprint
- Model shortlist: Mistral 7B Instruct, Llama 2 13B (4-bit), Falcon 40B Instruct, Mosaic MPT-7B Instruct
- Timeline: 4-week POC with deliverables each week

Action items (recap): see metadata list above

Transcript body:
[15:00] Priya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, then we'll scope the POC.
[15:01] Elena: Hi, Elena here - Head of ML at Halcyon. We're looking to automate extraction of structured fields from research reports and run a customer-facing QA assistant in English and Spanish.
[15:02] Samir: Samir - infra. Need to know network/VPC options, NVMe usage, and whether data leaves our VPC.
[15:03] Marcus (SE): Awesome. At a high level Redwood can do hosted, dedicated, or private VPC. For the POC we typically run on hosted for speed, but if you need VPC we can do Redwood Private. There's a small setup lead time.
[15:04] Nora: Timeline-wise we want a demo to stakeholders in ~4 weeks and a decision after that.
[15:05] Priya: Great. Let's talk success criteria - Elena, what would make this a win for you?
[15:05] Elena: Two pieces: extraction accuracy - we want at least 90% F1 on key entities (gene names, variant IDs, assay values) on our test set; and latency - ideally under 300ms median, P99 under 1 second for single-turn queries. Cost is also a factor - target is less than $0.15 per 1k queries at our projected scale, but that's flexible.
[15:06] Marcus: Noted. When you say queries what's the typical token length?
[15:06] Elena: Average prompt+context around 600 tokens, sometimes up to 2k for long reports. Multi-turn sessions for the QA assistant average 3 turns.
[15:07] Samir: Concurrent users - we see burst to 50 concurrent requests during business hours, steady state ~10 QPS.
[15:07] Marcus: That helps. For the POC we'll size the benchmark to mimic that: 50 concurrent, averages you mentioned, and run both single-infer and batched inference.
[15:08] Priya: On models, given your domain and multilingual needs, we recommend testing a short list of open models and one optimized quantized variant. Proposed shortlist: Mistral 7B Instruct, Llama 2 13B (q4_0 or q4_k), Falcon 40B Instruct, and MPT-7B Instruct. Thoughts?
[15:09] Elena: Curious why Llama 2 13B over Llama 2 70B? Cost/latency tradeoff?
[15:09] Marcus: Exactly. 70B gives quality but at much higher cost and latency. Our experience is 13B or 7B instruction-tuned models plus retrieval usually hit a sweet spot for extraction tasks. Falcon 40B often does well on instruction following but needs more memory. Also we can try an 8-bit or 4-bit quantized Llama 13B to reduce footprint.
[15:10] Nora: We care about Spanish - how do these models perform multilingual?
[15:10] Elena: Spanish coverage is non-negotiable. We need to test prompts in both languages.
[15:11] Marcus: Mistral 7B has decent English + some Spanish, Llama 13B tends to be stronger in multilinguals after RLHF, Falcon 40B can be mixed; we'll include bilingual prompt tests and evaluate per-language accuracy.
[15:12] Samir: For private data, does Redwood send logs offsite? Security is huge - SOC2, KMS, audit logs.
[15:12] Priya: We'll send the SOC2 and security pack. For hosted, customer data is logically separated and can be configured to not be used for model training; Dedicated gives more isolation; Private gives you full VPC control and customer-managed KMS/HSM. We'll include details in the pack.
[15:13] Elena: Perfect. For benchmarks - what metrics will Redwood run?
[15:13] Marcus: We'll run accuracy (F1 for extraction, exact match for key fields), hallucination checks (contradiction rate on a known-ground-truth subset), latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (tokens/sec), and memory/GPU utilization. We'll also run a small cost model for hosted vs dedicated.
[15:15] Elena: Do you do retrieval augmentation? For long reports that seems necessary.
[15:15] Marcus: Yes, we'll include a RAG baseline using your vector store (or we can use a temporary store) - run two modes: full context and retrieval + short context. Often RAG reduces hallucinations and improves latency for long docs.
[15:16] Priya: For the POC we'll propose this 4-week plan:
[15:16] Week 1: data collection and prep, Redwood sends harness and security docs; customer shares sample prompts and documents.
[15:17] Week 2: baseline runs on 3 models (Mistral 7B, Llama 13B q4, Falcon 40B) single-shot and RAG.
[15:18] Week 3: tune prompts, try quantized variants and batching strategies, evaluate cost/latency tradeoffs.
[15:18] Week 4: final runs, prepare report and demo to stakeholders.
[15:19] Elena: Sounds good. Will the harness support Spanish test sets?
[15:19] Marcus: Yes - we'll accept a bilingual CSV with prompts and ground truth. Also include expected rubric for scoring.
[15:20] Samir: On infra, if we go Private, what's the expected setup time?
[15:20] Priya: Private takes longer - typically 2-4 weeks for VPC peering and HSM integrations. For the initial POC we recommend hosted to move fast, then if you want we can migrate to Dedicated or Private for scale.
[15:21] Nora: Pricing ballpark - we're expecting a hosted pilot estimate vs a dedicated seat.
[15:21] Priya: We'll put together a pilot pricing estimate. For reference, the cost delta between hosted multi-tenant and dedicated GPU pools can be significant depending on throughput and model size. We'll include numbers in the follow-up.
[15:22] Elena: On model shortlist, could you justify including MPT-7B? It's smaller but we want to know if it keeps up on domain-specific terms.
[15:22] Marcus: MPT-7B is efficient and can be fine for extraction with strong prompt engineering. We'll measure absolute and relative gains. If it underperforms we can drop it and focus on 13B/40B.
[15:23] Priya: Any legal/procurement constraints?
[15:23] Samir: We'll need a DPA and standard security questionnaire completed before production. For POC it's usually lighter but procurement will want SOC2 and data handling notes.
[15:24] Priya: We'll attach a DPA template and the security questionnaire in the pack.
[15:25] Elena: For success criteria again: 90% F1 on entity extraction, Spanish parity within 5% of English accuracy, P99 latency under 1s, cost target ~ $0.12-0.18 per 1k queries. Also minimal hallucination on closed-list fields.
[15:26] Marcus: We'll design the scoring sheet accordingly and include hallucination heuristics.
[15:27] Nora: What do we expect for speed improvements via batching/caching?
[15:27] Marcus: Batching can improve throughput and reduce cost per token but may add latency. For your interactive assistant, continuous KV cache for multi-turn will help; we'll test caching for repeated contexts.
[15:28] Elena: Any recommendations on quantization? 4-bit wins on memory but sometimes hits quality.
[15:28] Marcus: Right - we'll run q4 and q8 variants for Llama 13B and compare. Sometimes q4_k or q4_0 retains most of the instruction-following behavior with big memory savings. We'll report delta in F1 and hallucination.
[15:29] Samir: Network: will we need to open egress to Redwood? If using hosted yes, for Private we can limit egress.
[15:29] Priya: Correct. We'll include network diagrams and suggested VPC peering steps.
[15:30] Elena: For evaluation, we'll also want qualitative examples - top 20 failure cases and example model outputs per model.
[15:30] Marcus: We'll produce a failure-mode report and recommended mitigations (prompt tweaks, retrieval, post-processing).
[15:31] Priya: Any blockers to start?
[15:31] Elena: We need to gather 50 sample reports and the scoring rubric; procurement needs SOC2 but that's fine.
[15:32] Priya: Great - next steps as discussed. We'll aim to kick off week of 2026-04-06 for the baseline runs.
[15:33] Nora: Can we get a short one-pager comparing expected latency/cost for each model?
[15:33] Marcus: Yes, Marcus to include a quick comparison table in the benchmark doc.
[15:34] Samir: Also include worst-case GPU memory usage for Falcon 40B so we can plan infra.
[15:34] Marcus: Will do.
[15:35] Elena: Any concerns about regulator requirements for healthcare data? Some reports have PHI.
[15:35] Priya: We can run the POC under Private or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS for production. For the POC we can white-list sample data and redact PHI if needed. We'll add notes in the security pack.
[15:36] Marcus: A quick note on evaluation: we'll run both automated metrics and human review for hallucination and domain correctness. Human review sample size ~200 examples.
[15:37] Elena: Good.
[15:38] Priya: Alright, recap of owners: Priya - security docs + DPA; Marcus - benchmark harness + model list + quick comparison; Elena - sample docs + rubric; Samir - network constraints.
[15:39] Nora: Looking forward. Thanks everyone.
[15:40] Priya: Thanks all. We'll send the pack and schedule follow-up.

End of call.

Notes on imperfections: occasional speaker mislabels and slight transcript noise (e.g., "K V cache" for KV cache, "q4 zero" for q4_0).
